subject: BrightHealth onboarding — initial org setup & service-account questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intro: BrightHealth onboarding + initial tenant notes

Hi Hannah / Sarah —

As discussed on the call, looping you both in to kick off the tenant/org setup for BrightHealth. Hannah will lead implementation from our side. Below are the high-level ask items we covered: 

- Create a production tenant for BrightHealth with one dev project and one prod project.
- API access: initial server-side service account + short-lived API keys for app testing.
- Invite list for first 6 users (CS + Eng + SRE).
- SSO: BrightHealth will provide SAML metadata (we discussed SAML-based SCIM if needed later).

Sarah — can you share the list of invitees and confirm whether you want single-tenant SSO or separate SSO for dev/prod?

Hannah — recommended next step: share a lightweight checklist and a timeline for the first two weeks so their security team can review.

Attachments: tenant-access-checklist.xlsx (starter checklist).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
[Attachment: tenant-access-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth onboarding — initial org setup & service-account questions

Hi Sarah — thanks Marissa. Quick plan from my side (short and actionable):

1) We provision tenant + two projects (dev/prod) on our end.
2) We create a service account for BrightHealth for server-to-server calls (can generate long-lived key OR recommend short-lived keys via our token exchange; see note).
3) We invite the first round of users (list below) w/ Owner/Editor/Viewer roles.
4) We exchange SAML metadata to enable SSO (we can walk through the IdP setup next week).

What I need from you to start:
- Final invite list (name, email, role: owner/editor/viewer).
- Decision on service-account key: long-lived JSON key OR use our recommended short-lived token flow (we can enable both, but short-lived is preferred).
- Any IP allowlist or outbound proxy details for your infra team.

Proposed timeline: tenant + basic invites within 48 business hours after we receive the invite list + service-account preference. SSO test environment next week (Wed/Thu).

I attached a short quickstart and annotated checklist. I also included an example of the policy template we typically apply to production projects.

Next step: Sarah, if you can reply with names, and Dev / Sean — please standby to provision the service account once Sarah confirms key preference.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0228
[Attachment: redwood-quickstart.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Action: BrightHealth tenant + service-account provisioning (timeline)

Dev / Sean — please action the items below for BrightHealth (deal RDW-BH-4521). Customer has confirmed invite list and prefers short-lived token flow. Timeline: complete provisioning and initial invites by 2026-09-16 EOD PT.

Tasks:
- Create tenant "brighthealth-prod" and project "brighthealth-prod/core" + dev project "brighthealth-dev".
- Provision service account "sa-brighthealth-inference" with scopes: token.exchange, inference.request, telemetry.write. Do NOT create a long-lived key; wire up the token-exchange endpoint per our short-lived token pattern.
- Apply baseline prod policy (RBAC: Org Admin = Sarah Lim, Editors = Ravi, Leila; Viewers = Priya + onboarding@brighthealth.com).
- Add SAML metadata to the tenant and schedule SSO test on Thu with Sarah (Hannah to coordinate).

Please reply with estimate (hours) and mark the ticket in Jira: ONB-721. I put the minimal checklist and quickstart in the thread (see attachments).

Thanks —
